requirements.requirement: On node1, sudo commands are recorded to /var/log/sudo-commands.log including the invoking user and a timestamp
requirements.summary: cmd-1d9e01e5c2704a5e shows a fresh sudo command (whoami) immediately appearing in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with syslog timestamp ('Sep 29 07:51:55'), hostname, and 'root :' user field. cmd-4a6db6cc50da4d6d repeats this after a full reboot with a fresh 'sudo id' command, confirming the mechanism (sudoers Defaults syslog=local2 + rsyslog local2.* routing) works both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Those sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log (/var/log/messages)
requirements.summary: grep -c 'sudo:' /var/log/messages returned 0 immediately after generating sudo activity (cmd-1d9e01e5c2704a5e) and again after reboot with fresh sudo activity (cmd-4a6db6cc50da4d6d), directly showing the local2.* stop directive prevents duplication into the general log both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: The configuration is durable/functioning after a restart (reasonable to expect for a logging control, though not explicitly stated in the instruction)
requirements.summary: Boot identity changed from f54d7366-... (cmd-fa48a62bccaa4068, pre-restart) to d9d11468-... (cmd-b403501605ff4c73, cmd-4a6db6cc50da4d6d, post-restart), confirming a real reboot occurred. Post-restart, the sudoers and rsyslog drop-ins were still present, rsyslog was active, and a fresh sudo command logged correctly to sudo-commands.log while remaining excluded from /var/log/messages, directly demonstrating the healthy pre-state, a bounded disruption (reboot with a connection-timeout poll), and recovered functioning state.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task: sudo commands on node1 are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp via a syslog=local2 sudoers directive routed by a dedicated rsyslog rule with a stop action, and verified excluded from /var/log/messages. The executor additionally ran a full reboot cycle showing pre-restart boot identity, disruption, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered/functioning logging and exclusion behavior, providing strong durability evidence beyond the literal instruction. The only shortcoming is a handful of unremoved staging/marker files left in /tmp.
limitations: Evidence is based on captured command outputs only; live system state was not independently inspected.
Leftover temp files (/tmp/99-sudo-logging, /tmp/49-sudo-commands.conf, /tmp/pre-restart-marker.txt, /tmp/reboot.log) were not cleaned up, a minor hygiene gap not affecting task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were directly tied to the task: installing the sudoers drop-in and rsyslog conf (cmd-1d9e01e5c2704a5e), creating/permissioning the log file (same command), restarting rsyslog to apply config, and the reboot/verification cycle (cmd-fa48a62bccaa4068, cmd-b69ce8b0b77f4cbb, cmd-4a6db6cc50da4d6d). No troubleshooting experiments or unrelated mutations were observed. Minor residue: staging files /tmp/99-sudo-logging and /tmp/49-sudo-commands.conf (used as install sources for cmd-1d9e01e5c2704a5e) and /tmp/pre-restart-marker.txt plus /tmp/reboot.log (from cmd-fa48a62bccaa4068 and cmd-b69ce8b0b77f4cbb) were never cleaned up and are visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. These are low-risk, non-sensitive, bounded leftovers with no security or functional impact, but they were not restored/removed, so hygiene is not perfect.
